limits: Reads: config 8,388,608 B and platform/preferences 131,072 B (DomainResourceLimits), snapshot 4 MiB, events tail 1 MiB / 20,000 rows, journal 1 MiB / 4,096 rows, Info.plist 1 MiB, executable 512 MiB. Larger is too_large and unproven.

Commands: /bin/ps, /usr/sbin/lsof, /usr/bin/curl, and /usr/bin/codesign in preflight only; 10 s timeout (curl 25 s, codesign 60 s), 4 MiB output. Only this tool's own timed-out child is killed, never Conduit.
Waits: 45 s per owner action, 20 s settle for journal and events, 0.25 s poll. Every duration includes the owner's reaction.

snapshot.json has no timestamp of its own; freshness is its mtime at or after the phase boundary. Baseline boundary: the --since launch epoch, else when this tool started; reopen: just before the Open prompt; Stop/Start/Quit: the prompt.

Event counts are since the phase boundary by event timestamp. They are complete only when a row older than the boundary is still in the read window (the 1 MiB events file truncates on rotation); an absence claim such as no helper failure needs that.
Journal checks count platform-state.json non-marker records only. They prove neither per-service physical restoration nor global PAC absence. User PAC priors are never read, judged or changed.
HTTPS success and Kerberos/helper events are recorded side by side; neither is claimed to cause the other.
Process identity is ps comm equal to the bundle's CFBundleExecutable path; the serving PID is the single lsof listener on the snapshot's loopback proxy port.
Connections rows are the owner's attestation, not tool evidence.
scope: Installed signed 0.6.1 smoke for the pool/auth/fixture fixes: owner Start, Stop, Start, Quit, reopen and Start, with process, listener, file-hash, structured snapshot/event/journal observations and one HTTPS request through the loopback proxy. No claim of per-service physical restoration, global PAC absence, DNS or split-DNS, autostart, or product-only Quit duration.
